original_question: For an ordinal η, is the Banach space C([0, η]) Plichko only in the case η < ω2?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.10 (Kalenda): "Is C([0, η]) Plichko only for η < ω2?"
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem the paper reiterates: it has the right space C([0, η]), the right parameter η (an ordinal), the right property (Plichko), and the right cutoff ω2. In fact, it is almost verbatim the formulation of Problem 6.10.
missing_details: [0, η] should be specified as the ordinal interval endowed with its order topology.
C([0, η]) should be specified as the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0, η], equipped with the supremum norm.
"Plichko" should be unpacked: in the paper, this means λ-Plichko for some λ ≥ 1, i.e. admitting a countably λ-norming Markushevich basis.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether this holds for every ordinal η.
The draft does not make explicit the nearby context that the stronger property "1-Plichko" is already known to fail for every η ≥ ω2; the open issue is whether mere Plichko can still occur there.
The draft omits the section-level motivation: the problem is posed in connection with the complemented-subspace heredity problem for Plichko spaces.
refined_question: For every ordinal η, where [0, η] is endowed with the order topology and C([0, η]) denotes the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0, η] with the supremum norm, must C([0, η]) be Plichko—that is, admit a countably λ-norming Markushevich basis for some λ ≥ 1—only when η < ω2?
justification: The draft is already essentially the paper’s official formulation: Section 6 restates Kalenda’s open problem exactly as "Is C([0, η]) Plichko only for η < ω2?" The only additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are the standard topology on the ordinal interval [0, η], the Banach-space structure on C([0, η]), and the paper’s definition of "Plichko." The surrounding paragraph explains why the question is sharp at the Plichko level: Kalenda had already shown nonexistence of countably norming M-bases for all ordinals κ ≤ η < κ·ω with κ regular, but it remains unknown whether this extends to every η ≥ ω2; moreover, the paper notes that C([0, η]) is already known not to be 1-Plichko for η ≥ ω2, so one should not strengthen the question beyond the Plichko level.
